title: virginia conservator handbook 001
instruction:
You are Naledi Gauthier, a lawyer at Sandpiper Laboratories' medical-legal partnership, preparing a handoff for Ursula Laurent, a frontline employee at Ironvale Provisions who has been appointed conservator for Javier Oduya after his brain injury left him unable to manage money. Ursula has no legal or accounting background and will prepare Javier's annual accountings without anyone from the partnership beside her. Using the attached `virginia_conservatorship_authority.pdf`, prepare `javier_oduya_conservator_handbook.docx` and `javier_oduya_accounting_workbook.xlsx` in the top level of the working directory. The handbook should be a plain-language, source-based guide she can follow the first time, with worked examples that use the same figures as the workbook. It must address the ordinary fiduciary decisions that are most likely to cause trouble: paying Javier's rent from Ursula's own account and seeking reimbursement later, a proposed gift to Javier's daughter, prudent handling of his money, records and receipts, and the annual accounting itself. Ursula is already asking what “personal expenses” means, because she uses that phrase for both her own household costs and Javier's ordinary living costs; make the meaning unambiguous before relying on it. She also wants to know what to do if a bank statement, receipt, signature, or other required part of the accounting cannot be obtained before filing, rather than assuming every filing will be complete. Apply the Commonwealth of Virginia law stated in the authority file as of January 1, 2025, and distinguish a rule from a practical safeguard or an example. Do not give system click-throughs, tax advice, investment recommendations, or advice about changing the court appointment. Keep the handbook to no more than eight pages, use accessible language without omitting legally important limits, and end with a usable pre-filing check rather than a list of future research tasks. The workbook must be usable for the worked examples, preserve source records and explanations for adjustments, and use a worksheet named exactly `Annual Accounting`; both files must agree on every figure they share.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/virginia_conservatorship_authority.pdf` — Offline source authority containing the applicable Commonwealth of Virginia conservatorship, fiduciary-accounting, recordkeeping, court-approval, and filing provisions in force on January 1, 2025.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `javier_oduya_conservator_handbook.docx` — A plain-language doctrinal handbook for Ursula Laurent, including source-based rules, cautions, a contingency path, and worked accounting examples. (Top-level working-directory file; no more than eight pages when rendered; accessible to a reader with no legal or accounting background; must distinguish legal requirements, practical safeguards, and examples; must use the names and facts in the request without inventing unsupported case facts.)
- `javier_oduya_accounting_workbook.xlsx` — A usable annual-accounting workbook supporting the handbook's worked examples, with transaction detail, reconciliation, explanations, and a pre-filing review area. (Top-level working-directory file; include a worksheet named exactly `Annual Accounting`; figures, labels, and example transactions must agree with the handbook; formulas should calculate totals and identify unexplained or unsupported entries; do not include live personal identifiers.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

materials.text:
Virginia Conservatorship Authority Digest
Commonwealth of Virginia • provisions in force as of January 1, 2025


Purpose and source
This offline digest consolidates the Virginia statutory provisions used for the conservator communication product. It is a source
extract/digest, not a case-specific order. Section references identify the governing provisions; the court appointment and any later
order control where more specific.


1. Fiduciary role and limits — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1200, 64.2-1205
A conservator is a fiduciary appointed to manage the estate of an incapacitated person. The conservator acts for the protected person
and under the authority and limits of the appointment and applicable law; the conservator does not become the owner of the protected
person’s property or obtain unlimited control over the person’s identity or ordinary life decisions.


2. Estate property, care, and prudent management — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1206
The conservator shall take possession of, manage, and protect estate assets for the protected person, applying income and principal
for the person’s needs and proper administration. Fiduciary conduct requires care, loyalty, preservation of value, reasonable liquidity
for needs, and avoidance of self-dealing or unnecessary risk. Estate property and fiduciary records must be kept identifiable and
separate from the fiduciary’s property.


3. Inventory and records — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1209, 64.2-1212
A conservator must identify estate assets and file the required inventory. The fiduciary must keep complete, accurate records and
vouchers sufficient for review by the Commissioner of Accounts or court, including statements, receipts, invoices, confirmations, and
court papers. Records must be produced when required.


4. Accounts and reconciliation — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1210, 64.2-1211
The conservator files an account with the Commissioner of Accounts for each required accounting period. An account reports the
beginning balance, receipts, disbursements, and ending assets/balance, with supporting vouchers and statements. The figures must
reconcile: beginning balance + receipts − disbursements = ending balance. The first account is generally due six months after
qualification; later accounts are generally annual and due within four months after the period closes, subject to the
court/Commissioner’s instructions and any applicable extension procedure.


5. Gifts and extraordinary transactions — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1208
A conservator may not make a gift of estate property merely because it seems generous, benefits family, or reflects what the
protected person might have wanted. A gift or other extraordinary disposition requires the legally required prior court authority; obtain
that authority before transferring money or property. Approval does not replace accurate records or reporting.


6. Reimbursement and compensation — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1213
A fiduciary may seek reimbursement for a genuine estate expense and may receive compensation only as permitted by law, the court,
or the Commissioner. Each amount must be reasonable, connected to estate administration or the protected person, and supported
by a clear record. A personal withdrawal is not made proper by labeling it reimbursement.


7. Conflicts and integrity — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1212
The fiduciary must act loyally for the protected person. A transaction benefiting the conservator or a related person presents a conflict
and should be held, disclosed, and handled only with the authority required by law or court. A missing document is not permission to
invent, backdate, conceal, or silently omit a transaction; disclose the gap and preserve proof of follow-up.


8. Filing problems and extensions — Va. Code §§ 64.2-1210, 64.2-1212
If an account cannot be completed or a required record is unavailable, the fiduciary should document the specific gap, request the
missing item, keep interim proof, and promptly contact the Commissioner of Accounts or court about the applicable filing or extension
 process. Do not ignore the due date or file a knowingly misleading account.

Prepared as the sole supplied authority for virginia_conservatorship_authority.pdf; as-of date: January 1, 2025.

gold.text:
Javier Oduya
Conservator Handbook
Prepared for Ursula Laurent • Naledi Gauthier, Sandpiper Laboratories medical-legal partnership
Commonwealth of Virginia law as of January 1, 2025
Purpose. A first-use guide for managing Javier’s estate and preparing a recurring annual accounting. It is based only on virginia_conservatorship_authority.pdf; the court appointment and later orders control if more specific.
LEGAL REQUIREMENT
The authority digest states what Virginia law requires. It cites statutes at the rule.
PRACTICAL SAFEGUARD
A workflow suggestion that reduces error; it is not a new legal power.
1. Your role and the words we will use
Rule — A conservator is a fiduciary managing Javier’s estate under the court appointment and Virginia law (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1200, 64.2-1205). This is not ownership of Javier’s property and does not give Ursula unlimited control over Javier’s identity or ordinary life decisions.
Personal expenses (definition). In this handbook, “personal expenses” means Javier’s ordinary living or care costs—such as his rent, food, utilities, and prescriptions—when they are for Javier and documented. It never means Ursula’s household costs, her family’s costs, or a convenience purchase for her. Ursula’s own costs are not estate expenses unless a genuine, documented estate expense was paid by her and reimbursement is allowed under the authority.
2. Keep money separate
Rule — Keep Javier’s money in identifiable estate accounts and separate from Ursula’s funds (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1206). Commingling is a handling problem even if Ursula reimburses herself later; later repayment does not rewrite the original bank trail.
Rent example. The workbook shows $1,200 February rent paid from Ursula’s personal account. It is a Javier expense, but it is marked Partial and “reimbursement held pending documentation.” Do not silently reimburse. Preserve the personal receipt, date, amount, purpose, and proof Javier’s estate benefited; record the event and handle any reimbursement only as a genuine estate expense with clear support and whatever authority the governing process requires (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1213).
Safeguard. Use a separate account register, save monthly statements, and label every entry before moving money.
3. Spend only for Javier or administration
Rule — Disbursements must serve Javier or proper administration of his estate and have a traceable purpose (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1212). Prudence means preserving value, keeping reasonable liquidity for needs, and avoiding unnecessary risk; it does not authorize speculative investments, unsupported cash, personal purchases, or “because funds are available.” This is a standard, not investment advice.
Gift to Javier’s daughter. A family relationship or good intention is not authority. Hold the proposed gift: make no transfer of money or property until the legally required prior court authority is obtained (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1205, 64.2-1208). Even if approved, report it accurately; approval never substitutes for records.
Conflicts and cash. If a transaction benefits Ursula or a related person, stop and disclose the conflict before acting. For cash withdrawals/payments, record date, amount, recipient, purpose, and receipt or other proof; unsupported cash activity is an exception, not a shortcut.
4. Record every receipt and transaction
Rule — Keep complete records and vouchers available for review (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1209, 64.2-1212): bank statements, receipts, invoices, confirmations, lease or care papers, court papers, and reimbursement support. Store them by accounting period and transaction reference so another person can retrieve them.
Classify correctly. Pension, interest, dividends, refunds, and other money received for Javier are estate receipts and need support. A refund that reverses a prior payment is an adjustment to that expense, not a brand-new source of wealth. A transfer between Javier’s own accounts is a transfer—not receipt or expense—and must be excluded from those totals. Never invent, backdate, or conceal a receipt, signature, authorization, or explanation.
5. Annual accounting: the repeatable method
Timing rule — The first account is generally due six months after qualification; later accounts are generally annual and due within four months after the period closes, subject to the Commissioner of Accounts/court instructions and any applicable extension procedure (Va. Code § 64.2-1210). Track the actual due date from your appointment and filing instructions; do not ignore an approaching deadline.
What to report. For each required period, report the opening balance, receipts, disbursements, ending assets/balance, and supporting records. The basic check is: opening balance + receipts − disbursements = closing balance. Enter each transaction in the workbook; its formulas calculate totals and flag mismatches or partial support.
Worked example (same rows and figures as Annual Accounting).

The proposed gift is $0 because no transfer was made. The February rent paid personally remains a documented exception until handled through the proper reimbursement path; it is still included as a disbursement in this illustrative reconciliation only because the estate expense occurred and is disclosed.
6. If something is missing or the deadline is near
Contingency path. Do not guess. (1) Identify the exact transaction/period and missing item (statement, receipt, signature, or explanation). (2) Request it promptly and keep proof of the request. (3) Mark the workbook Support status as Partial, Missing, or Requested and explain the gap. (4) Before filing, disclose the unresolved item and contact the Commissioner of Accounts or court about the applicable extension or filing procedure (Va. Code §§ 64.2-1210, 64.2-1212). Never fabricate, backdate, conceal, or silently omit. A court approval request, if needed, is separate from and does not cure the recordkeeping duty.
7. Pre-filing check — stop only when each answer is yes
☐ The accounting period and due date are written down from the appointment/instructions.
☐ Opening balance agrees to the prior closing balance and bank evidence.
☐ Every receipt and disbursement has date, amount, source/payee, purpose, and record status.
☐ Transfers between Javier accounts are labeled Transfer and excluded from totals.
☐ The formula reconciliation difference is $0.00 (status OK), or every exception is disclosed and addressed through the proper process.
☐ No personal expense of Ursula or her household is included; any reimbursement is genuine, documented, and authorized as required.
☐ The proposed daughter gift remains on hold unless prior court authority exists, and any approved transaction is reported.
☐ Statements, receipts, invoices, confirmations, court papers, and required signatures/certifications are retrievable; missing items are listed with follow-up proof.
☐ The account is truthful: nothing is invented, backdated, concealed, or silently omitted.
Source: virginia_conservatorship_authority.pdf (Commonwealth of Virginia provisions, as of January 1, 2025). This guide does not provide tax advice, investment recommendations, system click-throughs, or advice about changing the appointment.

spec.professional_context: This is a source-based Virginia conservatorship communication product for a non-lawyer fiduciary who must prepare recurring annual accountings independently. The main risk is not arithmetic alone but translating fiduciary rules into instructions that do not authorize conduct the law does not permit.
difficulty_sources: Translate source-based fiduciary and accounting rules into plain language without changing their legal effect.
Resolve the ambiguous term “personal expenses” for a non-lawyer audience.
Provide a defensible path when records or filing components are unavailable.
Create two usable deliverables whose worked figures, categories, and controls agree exactly.
Apply a named-jurisdiction rule set as of a stated date while minimizing sensitive information.

source_file.construction: Create one offline PDF containing verified excerpts or a faithful source digest of the applicable Virginia provisions in force on January 1, 2025. Cover conservator authority and limits, fiduciary handling of estate property, separate accounts and records, annual accountings and timing, court approval for gifts or extraordinary transactions, compensation or reimbursement, and the treatment of incomplete or late filings. Include section citations and an as-of date. Do not include a worked answer, sample figures, or drafting instructions.
source_file.source_integrity: Use one clearly identified Virginia authority source or one consolidated official-source excerpt set. Keep the document sufficient to establish all legal predicates in the rubric without relying on internet access.

gold_instance.case_mapping: Use Ursula Laurent as conservator and Javier Oduya as protected person. Use Naledi Gauthier as the preparing lawyer, Callum Aubert as a court or filing contact only if needed, and Mahdi Voskresensky as a partnership reviewer only if needed. Use Sandpiper Laboratories as the medical-legal partnership context and Ironvale Provisions as the employer context. Do not add real identifiers or unnecessary medical facts.
gold_instance.worked_example: Construct a small, internally consistent annual accounting example with a stated opening balance, several ordinary receipts, ordinary beneficiary expenses including rent, at least one internal transfer, and a closing balance. Include one example of a conservator-paid expense that must be separately documented and one proposed gift that is held pending the legally required authority. Derive every total from the transaction rows; do not hard-code contradictory totals.
gold_instance.workbook_behaviour: Build the `Annual Accounting` sheet with an opening balance, transaction detail, classifications, support/status fields, calculated receipt and disbursement totals, a calculated closing balance, and an exception or reconciliation check. Additional sheets may support instructions or lookup values, but they must not contradict the named sheet. Formulas should remain inspectable and recalculate correctly.
gold_instance.handbook_content: Write a concise plain-language handbook with a definitions box for “personal expenses,” source-linked legal rules, practical safeguards clearly distinguished from legal requirements, a separate-funds explanation, prudence limits, gift approval treatment, records and conflict controls, timing, annual-accounting mechanics, the missing-record/deadline contingency path, and a pre-filing check. Include a worked example whose figures and transaction descriptions match the workbook exactly.
gold_instance.doctrinal_boundaries: For each material rule, preserve the corresponding limit: fiduciary management is not personal ownership; prudence is not permission for speculation or personal purchases; court approval is not a replacement for records; a family gift is not automatically authorized; reimbursement is not self-authorization; and an unavailable record is not permission to fabricate or conceal. Avoid tax advice, investment recommendations, system procedures, or advice about changing the appointment.
validation: Render the DOCX and confirm it is eight pages or fewer.
Open and recalculate the XLSX with an offline office library or office-compatible renderer.
Compare every shared example figure and transaction description across both deliverables.
Verify the legal rules and timing against the supplied authority.
Test that changing a workbook transaction changes the reconciliation or exception result.
Confirm no real identifiers, unsupported personal facts, or invented legal codes appear.
